tested_revision: working tree on top of cabf6f7 (round-6 fixes: identified-only boundary — planner rejection prevents ALL input, abortable inter-leg settles restore the 2 s stop-latency bound, receipt validator fails missing/empty input logs for turn-committing runs, manual-handoff proof upgraded to a decoded-command check; committed with this receipt)

criteria.expected: no gameplay input, paused receipt, stop_requested latched
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=0 presses=0; input-log records stop_requested at t=0.001 (detection latency 0.001 s) and no press records
criteria.negative_control: pre-gate runtime classifies before checking the stop file; the latch now happens in run() via _stop_check before any classification

criteria.expected: wait exits; zero recovery B/route writes after observation
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=1 presses=30 (identified-only law); STOP drops once turn 1 is RECORDED and turn 2's menu is up; stop event at t<60 s; zero late key writes; engine stays live below the paused run
criteria.negative_control: Astra round-3 repro: pre-fix runtime sent B plus a full re-drive after observing STOP (reproduced as the strict-press scenario's first failing run)

criteria.expected: remaining route keys suppressed; at least one press aborted; zero writes after observation
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=0 presses=5; the identified flow gates BETWEEN legs, so a STOP that lands between presses suppresses the next attempt entirely (no write, no abort record); no press STARTS after stop_requested and the RAW write stream shows zero writes after observation; detection latency 1.196 s after the abortable-settle fix (was 2.791 s)
criteria.negative_control: first run of this scenario on the pre-fix code reproduced Astra's exact escaped-press shape (recorded in docs/project-log.md 2026-09-17 round-3 entry)

criteria.expected: remaining identified-drive legs suppressed; no press/drive record starts after stop_requested (B-recovery is GONE in the identified-only contract: recovery routes are not RAM-identified and are banned)
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=1 presses=35; STOP dropped on the first NEW key write after commit 1 (turn 2's dialog drive underway, legs still ahead); zero key writes timestamped after stop_requested in the RAW write stream; detection latency 1.174 s after the abortable-settle fix (was 2.779 s)
criteria.negative_control: pre-round-6 the runtime fell back to B-recovery plus fixed routes on any unidentified state (Astra round 6 gap 3: an invalid snapshot must PREVENT input, the identified-move-invalid scenario proves zero presses now)

criteria.command: python tools/validate_transport_paths.py --scenario strict-press --out-root outputs/autobattle (evidence-window retry loop shares wait_progress stop_check with all supplemental waits)
criteria.observed: wait_progress threads stop_check into its inner pump (stop_when per packet cycle); all runtime waits pass self._stop_check; paused state reached in every stop scenario
criteria.negative_control: pre-fix supplemental wait (seconds=5.0, min_new_seeds=9999999) had no stop_check parameter at all

criteria.expected: cancellation wins; no new turn starts after the latched stop
criteria.observed: state=paused turns=0; STOP dropped as the first post-commit seed arrived; no turn event after stop_requested; detection latency 0.181 s
criteria.negative_control: pre-stop_when code measured 3.005 s detection latency (one full 3 s pump tick), over the contract bound; recorded in the limitations of the prior working tree

criteria.expected: actual CLI/finally/__exit__ keeps owned PID alive, disarms owned hooks, releases keys, detaches
criteria.observed: probe reproduces the CLI's exact finally semantics (flip session.keep_process BEFORE __exit__): emulator pid survived __exit__ (probe.json emulator_survived=true), breakpoints disarmed in _finish, no key writes owned (per-press scratch re-write), transport closed
criteria.negative_control: Astra's round-2 mocked-CLI repro: __exit__ still called stop()'s kill default because keep_process never reached the session

criteria.expected: actual cleanup terminates ONLY the owned process
criteria.observed: run reached a bounded terminal state (stalled after the tracked player fell; 3 turns), keep_process=False reached __exit__, owned pid 23268 terminated, port released; no other process touched (taskkill scoped to the owned pid inside stop())
criteria.negative_control: the leave-running variant with the same code path survives, proving the flag and not an accident decides the outcome

criteria.command: python tools/validate_transport_paths.py --scenario disconnect --out-root outputs/autobattle; python tools/validate_transport_paths.py --scenario guard-failure --out-root outputs/autobattle; guard failure observed live 2026-09-15 (a3 first-boot, name decode failure)
criteria.expected: no further gameplay input; truthful terminal reason AND a complete receipt on the guard-failure path (Astra round 4 gap 3: the CLI exited before writing run.json and passed a `reason` kwarg the event schema drops); the receipt validator must FAIL when input-log.jsonl is missing or empty for a run that committed turns (Astra round 6 gap 1: the validator never required the log, so deleting it passed validation)
criteria.observed: disconnect: state=connection_lost, stop event records 'transport lost', zero presses after failure; guard-failure scenario drives the REAL run_autobattle.main() with the faked session: exit code 1, run.json written on the guard-failure path (final_state=stalled, turns=0), the failure reason rides the stop event note, a start event precedes the stop so the lifecycle validator accepts the receipt, and no input records exist; round-6 repro: copied c2-live5's receipt dir, deleted input-log.jsonl — the strengthened validator FAILS with 'a run that committed turns must carry its raw write log', while real receipts, zero-input runs (identified-move-invalid), and the bare guard-failure stream still PASS; the runtime's event() now raises on schema-unknown kwargs and the start event actually carries input_log (the old schema silently dropped it)
criteria.negative_control: pre-fix CLI returned before any receipt and emitted stop with a dropped `reason` kwarg; the scenario's first run failed exactly that way (missing run.json + 4 accumulated stop events)

criteria.expected: emulator survives cleanup AND a manual player command visibly works on the handed-off battle (Astra round 4: agent-driven player input through the window is sufficient; no human required)
criteria.observed: decoded-command proof (round-6 gap 2): runner paused at turns=1, keep_process=True reached the real __exit__, emulator pid survived; the agent re-attached READ-ONLY (bare Gdb connection, key writes never cross it) and RESUMED the core (r6b/r6c lesson: the stub halts on connect and serves stale reads while running — a monitor must interrupt->read->cont); the player-command window was detected from RAM (decoded cursor at 0 with Marche's roster CT frozen across polls, +34.2 s after handoff); one window SendInput DOWN moved the DECODED command cursor 0->1 (Move->Action) — identity no battle animation can fake; stub key writes 30 before = 30 after: the detached session did not fight the player
criteria.negative_control: r6c recorded the honest no-op: input sent with no menu open changed the screen but not the decoded cursor (changed=False, FAIL) — the cursor byte, not the screenshot, is the proof

criteria.expected: STOP observed within 2 s outside an already-pending OS/transport call
criteria.observed: stop-before-start 0.0 s; stop-during-identified-drive 1.174 s; stop-coincides-with-progress 0.181 s; strict-press 1.196 s — all inside the 2 s bound after making the identified drive's inter-leg settles abortable (they measured 2.779/2.791 s with fixed sleeps, recorded as the failing case)
criteria.negative_control: measured 3.005 s (over bound) before the per-packet-cycle stop_when fix; left in project log as the failing case

live_runs.result: PASS kill: owned pid 79864 terminated, port released (rerun on final round-4 code)
PASS decoded-command manual input: read-only monitor detected the parked menu, one window DOWN moved the decoded cursor 0->1, zero stub writes after handoff

limitations: offline scenarios certify control flow and ordering with a scripted engine; the fake mirrors recorded shapes (commit-then-effects, key-poll-per-frame) but ROM semantics of individual bytes are outside C1's scope
transport reads inside press() use blocking socket timeouts (~0.2 s per packet); STOP observed there waits for the press cycle to finish (~1.2 s), within the 2 s bound

the manual-input monitor halts the core briefly around each RAM read (interrupt->read->cont): read-only from the game's perspective — no key write ever crosses the stub — but reads are not free-running
